A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same theoretical work. The complete main texts, Figure 1, equations, and Appendices A–G are readable and support matching retained material and identifying additions.

before.justification: v1 reports mathematical guarantees and proofs, including theoretical LASSO applications and an ElasticNet example in Appendix F.2. It contains no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical. Its new lower-bound construction and approximate-minimization proposition are mathematical results; the constructed instances are proof witnesses, not empirical observations.

M1.justification: Section 6.1 adds a bilevel-loss variant that minimizes validation loss over an epsilon-optimal training set instead of exact training minimizers. This extends the loss formulation while retaining the FOL framework and existing LASSO objectives.

E1.justification: Neither version reports datasets actually used for empirical training or evaluation. Weighted group LASSO, weighted fused LASSO, and ElasticNet remain theoretical applications; the new lower-bound instances serve a proof.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods experimentally. Comparisons with Goldberg–Jerrum and Balcan et al. concern mathematical guarantees, not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Neither PDF specifies an empirical evaluation protocol. The added approximation tolerance and lower-bound construction define theoretical settings, not revised experimental budgets, metrics, or procedures.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, sensitivity tests, robustness studies, or error analyses. The approximate-minimization extension is a theorem, and the existing analytical application examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experiments, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical tests. The retained PAC probability statements are theoretical guarantees rather than empirical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Neither version reports measured performance values, rankings, or experimental findings. The added asymptotic lower bound and approximation guarantee are mathematical contributions assessed under T1.

T1.justification: v2 adds Theorem 5.2's Omega(p d log Delta_f) training-loss lower bound on unrestricted parameter domains, with a bit-extraction and stabilization proof in Appendix D.2. Proposition 6.2 adds a guarantee for epsilon-optimal inner solutions. Theorems 2.5 and 4.1 also explicitly fix the quantifier-block count K and revise complexity expressions, with corresponding changes in Appendix B.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion add a distinct claimed contribution: the first general training-loss lower-bound construction, supporting tightness in some regimes. v1 supplied upper bounds and recovered existing special-case tightness through ElasticNet; the original multidimensional learnability and LASSO claims remain.

C2.justification: Appendix D.2 newly interprets the lower bound as establishing unavoidable dependence and partial tightness in suitable constant-p regimes. Section 6.1 identifies exact inner minimization as restrictive, while the fixed-K footnote qualifies the prior-bound comparison. The general bilevel minimax question remains open.

D1.justification: Neither version provides experimental implementation settings, hardware, runtime measurements, or access instructions for its own code or data. The added proof constants and constructions are mathematical details, not implementation disclosures.

R1.justification: v2 adds Balcan et al. (2024), Algorithm Configuration for Structured Pfaffian Settings, and positions the new lower bound relative to missing prior guarantees and Bartlett et al.'s bit-extraction technique. Nguyen and Nguyen's 2025-to-2026 citation change updates the same work rather than adding another.

P1.justification: v2 adds upper/lower-bound subdivisions in Section 5 and Appendix D, Section 6.1, and acknowledgments, alongside scattered language corrections and affiliation updates. The overall narrative and section sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: The template running header is replaced by the paper title, and the front matter gains conference publication formatting. Text and equations reflow around the additions. Figure 1 and its caption remain unchanged, and neither version contains tables.

improvement.justification: Theorem 5.2 and Appendix D.2 substantially strengthen v1's upper-bound account by supplying an original constructive lower bound and explaining unavoidable complexity factors. The approximation extension and explicit fixed-K qualification also improve applicability and precision. The general bilevel gap remains open, and Proposition 6.2 references Theorem 5.1 without clearly specifying the needed assumptions on the validation objective g. These limitations do not outweigh the substantial gain in theoretical completeness.
